history.rationale: Removes the conserved N-linked glycosylation site; deglycosylation can modulate assembly and entry, sometimes increasing replication in certain host contexts. Phenotype effect uncertain, so moderate confidence.
N154 is the conserved E glycosylation site; removing the glycan (N154Q) frequently reduces mammalian replication fitness, so confidence is lowered pending evidence.

PLM (1.00) and structure compatibility (0.51) support tolerance of N154Q, while weak MSA mutant frequency (0.029) cautions that the glycan-site residue is evolutionarily conserved. N154Q removes the conserved E glycan, a known fitness-relevant feature, so confidence is raised only moderately rather than strongly.

Loss of the N154 glycosylation motif can alter particle assembly and immune evasion; ESM-1v and ProteinMPNN both indicate high plausibility/compatibility while MSA is neutral, so it remains the lead candidate.
Hydrophobic-to-hydrophobic substitution in domain II that could stabilize the fusion machinery. Conservative, likely viable.
